note: Harness^2 (arXiv 2610.14224v1, 2026-10-09, preprint). Headline numbers on screen: 43 and 78 out of 100 (JobBench production case study, task 1 deliverable score, Figure 9, p. 12; base 43.1, composed 77.8, gain +34.7) and 11 points (WorkBuddy-Bench office tasks macro-average score gain for GLM-5 under OpenCode: Base 64.2 -> Harness2 75.7, +11.5 points, Table 1, p. 8; sec 3.2). All results are authors' measured evaluations; no baseline is stated that the paper does not give. Flops/compute caveat noted (Appendix F, p. 29).

claims.l01: Section 1, p. 1-2 & Section 2.1: Open-world agents accumulating uncoordinated changes to instructions and tools suffer from clutter and regressions across diverse subsequent tasks.
claims.l02: Section 1 & Section 2.1: Harness2 couples two improvement loops: task-level recursion (contrastive probing on the current task) and harnessing-level recursion (updating the continual improvement harness across tasks).
claims.l03: Section 4, p. 11, Figure 9, p. 12 & Appendix E.7, p. 27: JobBench case study: reconciling event schedule, roster, and budget files into interconnected deliverables.
claims.l04: Section 2.1, p. 3: Definition of execution harness: the prompts, tools, retrieval configurations, and guardrails surrounding the model (Definition 1, p. 3; Appendix D, p. 21).
claims.l05: Section 4, p. 11-12 & Figure 9: Base harness execution on JobBench task 1 missed cross-file discrepancies and scored 43.1 out of 100.
claims.l06: Section 1, p. 2 & Section 2.2, p. 4: In open-world deployment, the agent receives no ground-truth task feedback or ground-truth reward to verify task correctness.
claims.l07: Section 2.2.1, p. 4 & Appendix D, p. 22: Contrastive proposals generate candidate harnesses with complementary scopes: invariant (INV) for general work habits / guardrails, and domain (DOM) for task-specific rules.
claims.l08: Section 2.2.1, p. 5: Probing executes each candidate harness on the same task under matched model and environment configurations.
claims.l09: Section 2.2.1, p. 5: Composition examines behavioral contrasts across candidate trajectories, selectively merging supported edits into a successor harness.
claims.l10: Section 2.2.1, p. 5: 'Each decision is tied to a concrete observation rather than a presumed score gain.' Receipt 1.
claims.l11: Section 4, p. 11-12 & Figure 9: The composed successor harness re-executes, verifies outputs, and raises the score to 77.8 out of 100 (+34.7 gain).
claims.l12: Section 1, p. 2 & Section 2.1, p. 4: Continuously mutating active execution files without isolation leads to prompt bloat, tool interference, and failure on future diverse tasks.
claims.l13: Section 2.1, p. 4 & Section 2.3, p. 5-6: The execution harness is reset for the next task; the continual improvement harness updates its harness improvement library, retaining adopted harnesses and lessons.
claims.l14: Section 2.1, p. 4: 'the execution harness is the system being improved, and the improvement harness is the mechanism that improves it.' Receipt 2.
claims.l15: Section 3.2, p. 8 & Table 1: On WorkBuddy-Bench (office workflows across slides, sheets, docs), Harness2 raises GLM-5 macro-average score by 11.5 points (64.2 to 75.7) under OpenCode.
claims.l16: Appendix F (Limitations), p. 29: Extra executions and editor sessions for recursive proposals and probing increase inference compute and time. Resetting task-specific execution files preserves adaptability without degradation.
